messages.author: f581744926bf88aa
messages.subject: shiny error help!
parts:
hi all, 
i'm following the shiny tutorial and trying to replicate the simple boxplot with my own data. but i ran into this error:
non-numeric argument to binary operator
i tried to hardcode x1-x6 into the boxplot function and it works fine. but somehow "input$var" does not work inside boxplot function. any idea? thanks!

here is my code: 
ui.r
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  
  headerPanel("sample test"),
  
  sidebarPanel(
    selectInput("var", "variable:",
                list("x1"   = "x1", 
                     "x2"   = "x2", 
                     "x3"  = "x3", 
                     "x4" = "x4",
                     "x5" = "x5", 
                     "x6"  = "x6")
                )
  ),

  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("boxPlot")

 )
))

server.R code
shinyServer(function(input, output){ 
  output$boxPlot <- renderPlot({
    boxplot(input$var)
  })
})

messages.author: c8fe4075ec631c03
messages.subject: shiny error help!
parts:
Main panel output is called twice, once with input$var set to NULL.

Just add a test to NULL before you call box plot

if(is.null(nput$var))return(NULL)

You may find yourself doing that a lot, in shiny.
-Alex

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: shiny error help!
parts:
input$var is a string in this case, so you're effectively doing something like this:
  boxplot("x1")

I think you want to do this:
  boxplot(x1)

And to do that, you need to get the variable (using global env here, but you may want something different:
  get(input$var, envir = .GlobalEnv)

However, if your app will be publicly accessible, it's probably not a good idea to simply grab whatever variable the client asks for, because it's very easy for someone to simply change the input variable to anything, and they could potentially view almost anything in memory of your R process. You can avoid this by using if statmeents -  see here:
https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shiny-discuss/fe5kE6SUfM0/oceXTO41Q0UJ
